# Timestamp

A moment in UTC: seconds since the Unix epoch and a fraction, normalized.

```rux
pub struct Timestamp {
    pub seconds: int64;
    pub nanoseconds: uint32;
}
```

`Copy`. The value is `seconds + nanoseconds / 1e9` from 1970-01-01T00:00:00 UTC, and `nanoseconds` is always in
[0, 1e9).

## Fields

| Name          | Type     | Description                                       |
| ------------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| `seconds`     | `int64`  | Whole seconds since the epoch, carrying the sign. |
| `nanoseconds` | `uint32` | The fraction, in nanoseconds, always in [0, 1e9). |

<h3 id="since"><code>Since</code></h3>

```rux
pub func Since(self: &Timestamp, earlier: Timestamp) -> Duration?
```

The span from `earlier` to this moment, or `None` past a duration's range.
May be negative: the wall clock jumps, and two readings taken across a clock-set really can come back
reversed. That is information, not an error, which is the difference from [`Instant::Since`](/docs/api/time/instant#since).

| Name      | Type        | Description         |
| --------- | ----------- | ------------------- |
| `earlier` | `Timestamp` | the earlier reading |

**Returns**: the time between the two moments, or `None` when `earlier` is not earlier

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Time/Src/Timestamp.rux#L93)

<h3 id="is-in-calendar-range"><code>IsInCalendarRange</code></h3>

```rux
pub func IsInCalendarRange(self: &Timestamp) -> bool
```

Whether this moment falls inside the years the calendar spells, and so has an RFC 3339 text.
The bound is years 0000 through 9999, which is the range [`Date`](/docs/api/time/date) arithmetic already treats as the package's
own and the range RFC 3339's four year digits allow. A caller that must not meet a formatting failure asks
here first; one that renders through a placeholder learns the same thing as `ValueOutOfRange`.
Borrows the moment and leaves it untouched. Cannot fail; runs in constant time and allocates nothing.

**Returns**: true when the calendar form exists for this moment

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Time/Src/Timestamp.rux#L32)

## Implements Display

`Timestamp` conforms to `Display`.

<h3 id="write-display"><code>WriteDisplay</code></h3>

```rux
pub func WriteDisplay(self: &Timestamp, writer: &var TextWriter, spec: FormatSpec) -> ! FormatError
```

Writes the moment as RFC 3339 in UTC, or as the Unix second count under the `unix` style.
The calendar form is the default and the only one an unadorned placeholder produces: `1970-01-01T00:00:00Z`
rather than `0`. `rfc3339` and `iso8601` name that same form explicitly, and `unix` asks for the signed
second count instead — a value with two readings does not get to guess which one a caller meant.
A precision names exactly that many fractional digits, 0 through 9, and truncates, in either form. Without
one the fraction is written to the digits it has with trailing zeros trimmed, and omitted when it is zero.
Reports whatever the writer reported, `UnsupportedRequest` for a style other than the three named above or
for a precision past nine, and `ValueOutOfRange` for a moment outside years 0000 through 9999, which RFC
3339's four year digits cannot spell. The range is checked before anything is written, so a refused moment
leaves the destination as it was.

| Name     | Type              | Description                    |
| -------- | ----------------- | ------------------------------ |
| `writer` | `&var TextWriter` | the destination                |
| `spec`   | `FormatSpec`      | what the placeholder asked for |

**Returns**: success when the whole moment was accepted

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Time/Src/Timestamp.rux#L86)
